title: Read the graph
prompt:
Here is the portfolio's history as a commit graph, the same shape `git log --oneline --graph --all` draws in text. Arrows point from each commit to its parent.

:::figure The portfolio's commit graph
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 230" role="img" aria-labelledby="ex1">
  <title id="ex1">Five commits. 1a2b and 3c4d in a row. From 3c4d, one line goes to 5e6f and another to 7a8b. Merge commit 9c0d has parents 5e6f and 7a8b. main and HEAD point to 9c0d; the label hero points to 7a8b.</title>

You're on `main`. Which commits does `git log --oneline hero` list?
hints: `git log <name>` starts at the commit that name points to.
From there it follows parent arrows only. It never walks forward to children.
Start at the commit labelled `hero` and follow the arrows until you run out.
explanation: `git log hero` starts at `7a8b`, the commit the `hero` branch points to, and follows parents: `7a8b` → `3c4d` → `1a2b`. The merge commit `9c0d` is a *child* of `7a8b`, and Git never walks from parent to child, so it isn't listed. `5e6f` is on the other side of the fork and isn't an ancestor of `hero` either.

a.text: All five commits, because `hero` was merged into `main`.
a.why: Merging made `hero`'s commits reachable from `main`, not the other way round. `git log hero` starts at `hero` and only walks backwards.

b.why: `git log` lists the starting commit and every ancestor, not one commit. `git show hero` would print only `7a8b`.

c.why: Correct. Start at `7a8b` and follow parents: `3c4d`, then the root commit `1a2b`.

d.why: `9c0d` is a child of `7a8b`. Commits don't know their children, so `git log` can't reach it from `hero`.
